slides.0.title: Viticulture and climate: drought, fire and organic
slides.0.subtitle: Climate pressure in Languedoc-Roussillon is favourite Diploma essay material
slides.1.title: Drought and yields
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Pyrénées-Orientales
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Pleinchamp (8 Nov 2024): dry for 30 months, with some plots giving no more than 500 kg/ha of grapes, about 3–4 hL of wine, and sometimes not covering machine-harvest costs
slides.1.highlights.1.title: 2022 and 2023
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Decanter: 2022 was hot and dry, with low yields in Faugères, 30% less at Domaine de Cébène and localised hail at the end of June in Pic St-Loup; in 2023 a late-August heatwave had four days above 40°C, berries shrivelled and yields collapsed, and Coupe-Roses in Minervois recorded only 250 mm of rain for the season
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Irrigation
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Wikipedia (dated): AOC and EU rules prohibit irrigation in principle, and the French government relaxed some rules in December 2006; check official texts for current detail
slides.1.content: Drought is the chronic problem; heatwaves and hail are the shocks.
slides.2.title: The 2025 Corbières wildfire
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Scale
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Decanter (14 Aug 2025): the fire started near Montlaur in the Aude, burned more than 17,000 ha, killed one person and injured more than 20; smoke and ash reached Narbonne
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Vineyard impact
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Early estimates put 800–900 ha of vines inside the perimeter and another 400–500 ha at risk of smoke taint (Jean-Marie Fabre of Vignerons Indépendants; final figures could be lower); Clos de l'Anhel lost about 90% and the Cellier des Demoiselles cooperative had 80% affected, including vines more than 60–70 years old
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Reading the numbers
slides.2.highlights.2.content: 800–900 ha is the fire perimeter, not confirmed losses; the subtitle says "in decades" while the body says "in more than 70 years", so we do not compare them
slides.2.content: Lost old vines cannot be replaced by replanting, which is the true cost of fire for old-vine regions.
slides.3.title: Organic and sustainability
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Organic weight
slides.3.highlights.0.content: BKWine (7 Aug 2024): Occitanie holds 34% of France's organic vineyards; Decanter (2018): Occitanie's 28,642 ha was about a third of the national total. Both measure the share of French organic vineyards
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Appellation examples
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Decanter (2018): in Terrasses du Larzac 85% of independent growers are organic or converting, covering 80% of the area; in Faugères 58% of domaines covering 40%; Gérard Bertrand has 15 properties over 920 ha, about 80% biodynamic or converting
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Disease-resistant varieties
slides.3.highlights.2.content: SevenFifty (sponsored): disease-resistant varieties were officially recognised for winemaking in 2021; the Institut Agro Montpellier studies 275 varieties, hybrids and rootstocks. HVE is not organic
slides.3.content: The denominators differ, so say clearly which share you mean when citing.
slides.4.title: Old vines and adaptation
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Defining old vines
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Wine With Seth defines old vines as 50 years and older, while Chile's VIGNO requires 30 years, which are different standards
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Management
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Carignan left unchecked can reach 200 hL/ha and must be controlled by short pruning and green harvest (Wine With Seth); naturally low old-vine yields help explain Fitou's average of about 40 hL/ha, the lowest of the Languedoc AOCs
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Adaptation paths
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Discussable paths: drought-tolerant varieties and rootstocks, cooler altitude and aspect, new disease-resistant varieties and organic farming to cut inputs; each has costs and limits worth writing about
slides.4.content: A Diploma essay gains marks by setting opportunity and cost side by side.
The August 2025 wildfire hit which part of Languedoc?
A. Corbières in the Aude (near Montlaur)
B. Pic Saint-Loup in the Hérault
Corbières in the Aude, starting near Montlaur (Decanter).
How many days above 40°C did the late-August 2023 heatwave have?
How long had the Pyrénées-Orientales been dry by November 2024?
What is Fitou's average yield, roughly?
About 40 hL/ha, the lowest of the Languedoc AOCs (Wine With Seth).
How does HVE relate to organic?
A. HVE is not organic and may still use some synthetic chemicals
C. HVE is stricter than organic
HVE producers are not counted as organic (Decanter).
Terrasses du Larzac (Decanter, 2018): what share of independent growers were organic or converting?
